Answer: A
Reason: The initial chest X-ray (Figure 1a) shows a large left-sided mediastinal mass with significant opacity and mediastinal shift to the left, indicating volume loss/collapse. The post-treatment X-ray (Figure 1b) demonstrates a marked reduction in the mass size, resolution of the mediastinal shift (midline trachea), and re-aeration of the left lung fields, consistent with re-expansion of the previously collapsed lobe.
